title: Score-based Generative Modeling for Conditional Independence Testing

problem.claim: Conditional independence testing is challenging, particularly in high-dimensional settings.

gap.claim: Existing generative-model CI tests can suffer from inaccurate conditional-distribution modeling and unstable training.

contributions.claim: A CI testing method based on score-based generative modeling.
A sliced conditional score-matching scheme with conditional Langevin sampling for generating null-hypothesis samples.
A goodness-of-fit stage for verifying generated samples and improving practical interpretability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present the score-based generative-model CI testing method as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method is reported to achieve precise Type I error control and strong testing power.
The authors report theoretical error bounds for modeled conditional distributions and a proof of CI-test validity.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to show significant outperformance over existing state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conditional independence testing is difficult in high-dimensional settings.
Existing generative-model approaches face conditional-modeling and training-instability problems.
The proposed method uses score-based modeling, sliced conditional score matching, and conditional Langevin sampling.
A goodness-of-fit stage checks generated samples and improves interpretability.
The abstract reports theoretical validity results and empirical gains on synthetic and real-world data.

source_observation.claim: The method combines score estimation, conditional sampling, and goodness-of-fit checking within one CI-testing pipeline.

interpretation.claim: Separating sample generation from post-generation verification may improve control and interpretability.

application.claim: For generative-model-based hypothesis tests, include an explicit verification stage for generated null samples.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the verification stage fails or how much it contributes independently.

unknowns: Specific datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
Theoretical assumptions and the form of the error bound are not specified.
Implementation details and computational costs are not described.
